prior_art_found.what: 'Mathematical Marbling' (Lu, Jaffer, Jin, Zhao, Mao) models combing actions as closed-form area-preserving transformations -- the forward stroke->pattern map, no full fluid solver needed
prior_art_found.snippet: This approach models combing actions in paper marbling using closed-form mathematical transformations, arguing that you don't need to run a full-blown fluid solver to accurately simulate a marbled pattern.

prior_art_found.what: Navier-Stokes marbling sims (IEEE 'Nondissipative Marbling') treat marbling as a 2D fluid-dynamics problem
prior_art_found.snippet: The marbling texture design process can be modeled as a 2D fluid-dynamics problem using Navier-Stokes equations to model the fluid evolution of the patterning process.

prior_art_found.what: Koopman operators are heavily applied to chaotic advection / mixing / data-driven prediction of chaotic flows (technique-family on sibling fluid-mixing domain)
prior_art_found.snippet: A finite-dimensional approximation of the Koopman operator using vector-valued, delay-embedded observables with nonlinearities treated as external forcings can provide accurate predictions for several Lyapunov timescales for chaotic systems.

results.exact_unused_slice: Using a LEARNED Koopman/evolution operator (kooplearn-style spectral, data-driven) to model the marbling comb-stroke sequence as a chaotic-advection dynamical map and forecast the resulting marbled figure. Existing marbling math uses analytic closed-form area-preserving / Navier-Stokes forward solvers, NOT a learned Koopman operator; existing Koopman-on-advection work targets generic mixing/turbulence, not the comb-stroke->figure marbling map.
results.honest_adjacency: BOTH axes touched: (app) marbling forward stroke->pattern simulation exists analytically and via Navier-Stokes; (technique) Koopman operator learning routinely applied to chaotic advection/mixing flows.
results.reasoning: Application is well-modeled but by analytic/PDE solvers, and Koopman learning is a standard tool for chaotic mixing -- the two have not been joined. Clear adjacency on both axes => not OPEN. The specific learned-Koopman x marbling-comb-stroke pairing is not published => not CLOSED.

prior_art_found.what: Interpretable, data-driven plasticity models built WITH symbolic regression (exact technique-family on plasticity/materials)
prior_art_found.snippet: an implicit symbolic regression technique has been developed to identify a plastic yield potential from homogenized finite element response data.

prior_art_found.what: ML prediction of Atterberg limits (liquid/plastic limit) and volume-change behavior from clay indices
prior_art_found.snippet: Studies have developed artificial intelligence models to predict Atterberg's limits, specifically the liquid (LL) and plastic limits.

prior_art_found.what: Closed-form clay plasticity-index models exist (R2=0.9982) linking slope/LL to PI -- analytic relation for bulk plasticity
prior_art_found.snippet: The relationship between average slope (20/LL) and plasticity index showed an R2 = 0.9982.

prior_art_found.what: Workability window for plastic forming of ceramics quantified vs water content
prior_art_found.snippet: Overall workability of a clay can be viewed as a coupling of the toughness of a 'normal consistency' clay and the range of water contents over which the clay can be effectively worked.

prior_art_found.what: Tactile sensing can read moisture/hardness/softness of deformable objects in robotics (adjacent sensing modality)
prior_art_found.snippet: Tactile sensors are devices that measure properties of objects through physical contact, including shape, texture, temperature, hardness, and moisture content.

results.exact_unused_slice: A symbolic / closed-form relation for the HAND TACTILE workability setpoint ('smooth = just right' felt by a potter) as a function of inter-particle plasticity -- i.e., the tactile/perceptual just-right point, NOT the bulk lab indices (LL, PL, plasticity index) or NIR bulk moisture %. Existing SR-plasticity and Atterberg-ML work models bulk geotechnical/ceramic indices, never the tactile setpoint.
results.honest_adjacency: BOTH axes touched: (app) clay plasticity vs water content is modeled extensively by closed-form index relations AND ML (Atterberg, workability window); (technique) symbolic regression is already used to build interpretable plasticity/yield models.
results.reasoning: Technique (SR on plasticity) and application (clay plasticity/workability vs water) both have dense prior art => far from OPEN. But all of it is bulk-index / instrumented, not the tactile hand-feel setpoint; the SR x tactile-setpoint pairing is unpublished => not CLOSED.

prior_art_found.what: Published CLOSED-FORM free-reed natural-frequency formula including tip-mass ratio K -- directly the metal-removal vs pitch relation
prior_art_found.snippet: f = 1/2pi x sqrt(X/L^2) x sqrt(E/D(1+4.1K)) ... K is the ratio between the mass at the end of the tongue and the mass of the tongue itself.

prior_art_found.what: Established tuning practice: filing tip (-mass, raise pitch) vs root (-stiffness, lower pitch) -- the exact craft rule
prior_art_found.snippet: It is common practice to tune a reed to a desired pitch by removing material from the tip (reducing mass and raising pitch) or from the root (reducing stiffness and lowering pitch).

prior_art_found.what: Cantilever/tuning-fork etching frequency-shift equations with position-dependent mass sensitivity (sibling vibration domain, closed-form)
prior_art_found.snippet: A game-changing equation during the etching of tuning forks and its verification through experiments.

prior_art_found.what: Closed-form / regression natural-frequency expressions for cracked & modified beams (material-removal analog)
prior_art_found.snippet: novel polynomial expressions have been developed to obtain natural frequencies as a function of angular velocity, slenderness ratio, cube radius and crack characteristics, formulated using multiple regression techniques.

prior_art_found.what: Existing accordion/free-reed tuning software (FFT phase-vocoder) for measuring per-reed pitch error (tool axis)
prior_art_found.snippet: musical instrument tuner specialized for accordion reed tuning with multi-pitch detection ... uses FFT with phase vocoder for sub-bin frequency accuracy.

results.exact_unused_slice: A SYMBOLIC-REGRESSION-DISTILLED inverse prescription -- 'how much metal to remove and exactly where along THIS reed to hit target pitch' learned from data -- as opposed to the existing analytic forward acoustic model. The forward relation (mass/stiffness -> frequency, tip vs base) already exists in closed form; the SR-from-data inverse filing-amount/location prescription per reed is the only unused slice.
results.honest_adjacency: Near-CLOSED. BOTH axes heavily touched: (app) closed-form free-reed frequency formula with tip-mass term AND the explicit tip/base filing rule are published; (technique) symbolic/regression closed-form derivation of beam/tuning-fork frequencies under material removal is standard, plus existing accordion-tuning tools.
results.reasoning: This is the weakest gap of the four: the technique x application essentially exists analytically (free-reed frequency formula + tip/base filing rule + cantilever etching equations). Held at NARROW (not CLOSED) only because no source SymTorch-style data-driven symbolic DISTILLATION producing an inverse per-reed filing prescription was seen; reserve weakly.
